chains.title: TCF7L2 loss-of-binding derepresses POU5F1B

links.claim: TCF7L2 occupies the variant in HCT116 and is expressed there; QBiC-SELEX with a CIS-BP-mapped LEF1 model gives z -4.66, effect -0.47, so the ref G allele binds more strongly. TCF7L2 is chosen over other occupied TFs because it has both HCT116 occupancy and an above-gate allelic QBiC-SELEX change in the ref direction.
The variant lies in active pELS EH38E3858447 with DNase, H3K27ac and CTCF signal, and active-element cofactors bind nearby; an allele-specific TCF7L2 change could alter enhancer output.

The alt T allele is associated with higher POU5F1B in colon transverse tissue, and POU5F1B is the top L2G gene. If TCF7L2 represses this element, weaker TCF7L2 binding on T would raise POU5F1B. POU5F1B is not a common essential in HCT116, so this is a risk-expression model rather than a dependency model.
HCT116 expresses TCF7L2 and has TCF7L2 ChIP-seq over the variant; the POU5F1B eQTL is in colon transverse tissue, supporting a colorectal context.

The T allele is the colorectal-cancer risk allele. The chain predicts that T reduces TCF7L2 binding, relieves repression of POU5F1B, raises POU5F1B, and thereby increases colorectal-cancer risk. E37 weakens a simple POU5F1B oncogenic-dependency interpretation.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy is higher on ref G than alt T at chr8:127401060 in colorectal cells.
TCF7L2 depletion or mutation of the TCF7L2 site increases POU5F1B or enhancer reporter activity if TCF7L2 is repressive here.
The alt T allele increases POU5F1B expression in colorectal cells, consistent with derepression.

TCF7L2 depletion or site mutation does not increase POU5F1B or enhancer activity, arguing against TCF7L2 repression here.
The POU5F1B eQTL/L2G signal is explained by a linked variant rather than this base.

The variant lies in an active pELS enhancer-like element, so an allele-specific change in NR2F2 binding could alter enhancer output.

The alt T allele is associated with higher POU5F1B in colon transverse tissue, and POU5F1B is the strongest L2G gene. If NR2F2 activates this element, increased NR2F2 binding on T would raise POU5F1B.
NR2F2 is expressed in HCT116, but direct NR2F2 occupancy at this base is shown only in HepG2; this chain requires unshown colorectal-cell occupancy.
The T allele is the colorectal-cancer risk allele; the chain predicts that T increases NR2F2 binding, activates POU5F1B, and promotes colorectal cancer.

chains.title: HNF4A activation of POU5F1B
chains.cell_type: liver/HepG2-like context; HCT116 expression is low

links.claim: HNF4A is predicted to bind the alt T allele much more strongly than ref G: QBiC-SELEX gives z 53.69, effect +1.968, with a strong site. However, HNF4A is only 2.95 TPM in HCT116 and its ENCODE peak over the variant is in HepG2/liver, not HCT116, so disease-relevant occupancy is not established.
The variant lies in an active pELS enhancer-like cCRE, allowing a binding change to affect enhancer activity.
The alt T allele is associated with higher POU5F1B in colon tissue, and POU5F1B is the top L2G gene. If HNF4A activates POU5F1B, preferentially increased HNF4A binding on T would raise POU5F1B.
This chain requires HNF4A activity in colorectal cells, but the evidence places HNF4A occupancy in HepG2/liver and gives low HCT116 expression; the cell-type link is weak.
The T allele is the colorectal-cancer risk allele; the chain predicts that T increases HNF4A binding, activates POU5F1B, and increases colorectal-cancer risk in HNF4A-expressing cells.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr8:127401060:G>T, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 64 occupied (19 with a strong site), 5 of 133 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 6 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 497 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 6 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
